about: Research sheet for the Maine county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Maine
phones_sentence: Veterans office phones and addresses come from the Maine Bureau of Veterans’ Services’ field office pages. Most offices ask you to call for an appointment.

offices.source_title: Maine Bureau of Veterans’ Services: Field Office and Itinerant Office Locations
offices.note: Maine Bureau of Veterans’ Services veterans service officers help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and VA health care enrollment at no charge.
offices.selection: Office address and phone from the Bureau’s locations page; counties served from each office’s own page (Augusta: Kennebec and Somerset; Togus: Kennebec and Lincoln). Two pages disagree: the locations page gives Augusta 207-287-9933 (also Togus’s number) and Machias 53 Prescott Drive, while the office pages give 207-287-7020 and 7 Court Street; the cards use the Augusta page’s number and the locations page’s Machias address, and say so. Caribou’s service area (Aroostook) comes from a search excerpt of its page. Knox and Waldo are named by no office page and show the Bureau’s central line. Itinerant visits are shown where an office page lists them.

programs.name: Maine veterans: Bureau of Veterans’ Services field offices for claims help
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension, survivor benefits and VA health care enrollment from the Maine Bureau of Veterans’ Services’ veterans service officers, in field offices in Augusta, Bangor, Caribou, Lewiston, Machias, Portland, Springvale and Togus.
programs.next_step: Call the field office for your county (choose a county above) or the Bureau’s central line, 207-287-7020, to make an appointment.
constraints: Offices are open Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.; most ask you to call for an appointment.

programs.name: Maine Area Agencies on Aging and Aging and Disability Resource Centers
programs.organization: Maine Office of Aging and Disability Services and the five Area Agencies on Aging
programs.description: Maine’s five Area Agencies on Aging are also its Aging and Disability Resource Centers: one-stop help for older adults, adults with disabilities and care partners with in-home, community and long-term care services, meals, caregiver support and Medicare counseling. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 877-353-3771 and choose your county, or choose a county above for its agency.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.
programs.phone_label: Maine Aging and Disability Resource Centers (877-353-3771)

sources.title: Maine Office of Aging and Disability Services: Area Agencies on Aging

programs.name: Medicare counseling (Maine SHIP)
programs.organization: Maine State Health Insurance Assistance Program, through the Area Agencies on Aging
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from Maine’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, sponsored by the Office of Aging and Disability Services, the five Area Agencies on Aging and Legal Services for Maine Elders: Part D and supplement plans, costs and help paying for Medicare.
programs.next_step: Call 877-353-3771 (877-ELDERS1) and choose your county. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

programs.name: Maine Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Maine Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; Maine Adult Protective Services
programs.description: Advocacy for residents of nursing, boarding and adult foster homes and people receiving home care. Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of incapacitated or dependent adults 24 hours a day.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman at 800-499-0229. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation, call Adult Protective Services at 800-624-8404 or 207-287-1234, or use the online form. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

sources.title: Office of the Maine Attorney General: Older Mainers
sources.scope: Ombudsman 1-800-499-0229 and Adult Protective Services 1-800-624-8404 (24 hours); read in full.

sources.title: Maine Office of Aging and Disability Services: Adult Protective Services
sources.scope: Report by phone 1-800-624-8404 or 207-287-1234, TTY Maine Relay 711, or the online form; read in full.

programs.name: Free legal help for Maine veterans and older adults
programs.organization: Legal Services for Maine Elders; Volunteer Lawyers Project
programs.description: Legal Services for Maine Elders gives free legal help to Mainers 60 and older in many civil cases, including benefits, health insurance, powers of attorney, consumer problems, abuse and guardianship defense, with offices in Augusta, Bangor, Lewiston, Portland and Presque Isle.
programs.next_step: Call the Legal Services for Maine Elders Helpline at 800-750-5353 (207-623-1797 from out of state). Under 60? Call the Volunteer Lawyers Project: southern Maine 800-422-4293, northern Maine 888-956-4276.
constraints: Legal aid screens by age, income and case type.
programs.phone_label: Legal Services for Maine Elders Helpline (800-750-5353)

sources.title: Office of the Maine Attorney General: Older Mainers
sources.scope: Legal Services for Maine Elders: 1-800-750-5353 in state or 1-207-623-1797, age 60 and over, offices in five cities; read in full.

sources.title: Office of the Maine Attorney General: Finding an Attorney
sources.scope: Volunteer Lawyers Project lines for southern and northern Maine; search excerpt.

programs.name: VA health care in Maine
programs.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Maine Healthcare System
programs.description: Maine veterans are served by the VA Maine Healthcare System, centered at Togus (main telephone 207-623-8411), with clinics around the state.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Bureau of Veterans’ Services officer for help applying.
constraints: Ask about travel and community care options if the nearest clinic is far.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 16 counties have a Maine Bureau of Veterans’ Services route (14 named by a field office; Knox and Waldo use the Bureau’s central line), an Area Agency on Aging (five agencies), the statewide long-term care ombudsman and Alpha One.
coverage_note: Veterans contacts come from the Maine Bureau of Veterans’ Services’ field office pages. Area Agencies on Aging come from the Office of Aging and Disability Services. The ombudsman, Adult Protective Services and elder legal help lines come from the Attorney General’s Older Mainers page. Reviewed November 16, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
